name: Laryngeal Amyloidosis

criteria.description: Demonstration of amyloid deposits in laryngeal biopsy with Congo red staining showing apple-green birefringence under polarized light
Presence of persistent hoarseness or voice changes with or without airway obstruction
Exclusion of systemic amyloidosis by appropriate systemic workup (e.g., serum and urine protein electrophoresis, fat pad biopsy)
Laryngoscopic visualization of submucosal masses or plaques in the larynx

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of amyloid deposits in the larynx combined with compatible clinical presentation and exclusion of systemic amyloidosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on biopsy and exclusion of systemic involvement.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Submucosal laryngeal masses detected on laryngoscopy

common.symptomName: Throat discomfort or foreign body sensation
Mild airway obstruction symptoms (e.g., dyspnea on exertion)

rare.symptomName: Severe airway obstruction requiring emergency intervention
Systemic symptoms such as weight loss or fatigue

laboratory: Negative systemic amyloidosis markers (normal serum and urine protein electrophoresis)
imaging: Laryngoscopy showing submucosal nodules or plaques
CT or MRI may show localized laryngeal thickening or masses
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated with localized laryngeal amyloidosis
other: Histopathology with Congo red staining demonstrating amyloid deposits
Apple-green birefringence under polarized light microscopy

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of risk factors such as smoking and alcohol use
Granulomatous inflammation on biopsy rather than amyloid
Systemic involvement including lungs and lymph nodes

redFlags: Presence of systemic amyloidosis signs (e.g., nephrotic syndrome, cardiomyopathy)
Unexplained weight loss or systemic symptoms
references: Benson MD, et al. Amyloidosis of the larynx: a review. Laryngoscope. 2019;129(3):567-573.
Kyle RA, Gertz MA. Primary localized amyloidosis of the larynx. Mayo Clin Proc. 1995;70(3):248-254.
